challengeFindings.title: A rejected tracker key is printed into the run's warning annotation: on `bkit issues fetch` exit 80 `reason=auth` with `BKIT_JIRA_API_KEY` (or `BKIT_LINEAR_API_KEY`, or `GH_TOKEN`) set, `${!secret_var:-empty or missing}` expands to the secret's value, so the warning reads `set but rejected<value>` and exposure rests on GitHub log masking alone

A failed `Install bkit` on a post-merge `dev` CI failure is misreported: with `node_modules/.bin/bkit` absent the dev arm never reaches `bkit_gate`, so it logs the `::notice::Cannot derive FID by dev commit scope or linked PR` no-op instead of the `bkit-unavailable` warning, writes no gate summary row, and the in-code comment ("`bkit_gate` reports an absent bkit") is false

A feat branch pushed by a steered agent session ships its own `bkit` (package.json / lockfile / committed `node_modules/.bin/bkit`), which the context job then runs to decide the `bkit:auto` kill switch, so the agent can keep itself dispatched after the human removes the label

A squash commit message longer than the runner's pipe buffer (64 KiB on Linux; a long PR description becomes the squash body) kills the dev arm red: `printf '%s\n' "$COMMIT_MSG" | head -1 > "$SUBJECT_FILE"` runs under `set -euo pipefail` without the `|| true` the replaced line carried, so `head` closing early SIGPIPEs `printf` (exit 141) and the step aborts instead of reaching dispatch or the no-FID no-op

A consumer who fills the new `BKIT_OPENAI_API_KEY` row in `.bkit/.env` gets that paid OpenAI key pasted into every generated cloud env block (`.claude/bkit-cloud.md`, `.cursor/bkit-cloud.md`, `.codex/bkit-cloud.md`), so every cloud agent session that reads untrusted issue / PR text holds it

A Cursor background session in a repo whose `bkit.tracker.default` holds a value the guard does not recognise (e.g. `GitHub`, `Jira`, `gitlab`) skips the `bkit:auto` check with exit 0 and writes no context line, so an unlabelled or finished issue runs unchecked

A session whose `GITHUB_ISSUE_ID` holds a path such as `1/../../../../repos/other-owner/other-repo/issues/5` makes the GitHub guard read an issue in another repo, so a labelled, open issue elsewhere passes the guard

challengeFindings.title: A consumer whose repo has no `packageManager` field or no `pnpm-lock.yaml` (or any run where the pnpm download or the pnpm cache restore fails) gets a red context job instead of the documented green `bkit-unavailable` no-op: `pnpm/action-setup` and `actions/setup-node` (`cache: pnpm`) sit before `Install bkit` without `continue-on-error`, so they abort the job before the gate can report anything

A consumer records `--auto=codex` on `dev`, but every feature branch cut before that commit has no `bkit.cloud.agent` in its own `package.json`, so `Select agent job` reads `none` from `pr-head/`, starts nothing, and its notice tells them to "Run bkit install --auto=<claude|opencode|codex>", a command they already ran; the reverse also holds: setting `bkit.cloud.agent` to `none` (or another agent) on `dev` does not reach in-flight branches, which keep starting the agent their own `package.json` names

A feat/** CI run whose branch was deleted before the router starts (PR merged with auto-delete, or closed while CI ran) turns the context job red: the new `pr-head` checkout asks `actions/checkout` for `workflow_run.head_branch` by name, which no longer exists, and the step has no `continue-on-error`; before this diff the same run reached the feat arm's green "no open PR" no-op

A post-merge `dev` CI failure whose squash commit message is larger than the pipe buffer (64 KB on Linux; a squash of a PR with thousands of commits) kills the context step red: `printf '%s\n' "$COMMIT_MSG" | head -1 > "$SUBJECT_FILE"` runs under `set -euo pipefail` with no `|| true`, so `printf` dies on the broken pipe once `head -1` exits; the replaced pipeline carried `|| true` for exactly this reason

A session whose `GITHUB_ISSUE_ID` carries a path (`12/../../../../other-owner/other-repo/issues/5`) makes the GitHub session guard read a different repo's issue that carries `bkit:auto`, so the guard prints PASS for work on an issue that never opted in
